subject: v1.1 task 11.2 - Provider-client integration and bulk reads - test-quality re-review (attempt 2) of the correction round for TQ-11.2-1..6 and RC8 chunking, tests/ArrTags.Tests/ProviderInventoryCacheIntegrationTests.cs (20 cases)
assessment: Independent re-review after the correction round. I rebuilt the working tree, reproduced the full default suite (Failed 0, Passed 1407, Skipped 63, Total 1470) and the focused class (Passed 20, Skipped 0, Total 20), then verified every attempt-1 finding with mutation testing in a throwaway copy under /tmp (never in the repo). Every closure is genuine and mutation-sensitive: the provider-failure boundary now drives a real stale-but-usable entry and a real expired entry through the production reader (both directions fail under mutation); the Sonarr over-bound fallback test now fails when the fallback is disabled; the whole-library-retention tests fail when only one observation is retained (Radarr and Sonarr); the per-connection single-flight test fails deterministically (3/3) when the shared gate is removed; the repeated Sonarr episodeFileIds selector fails when only the first id is emitted; and the new chunking test fails when chunking is bypassed. The documented current-suite counts are refreshed and match my run. All 20 cases are unguarded [Fact]s that run in the shipping default configuration; no new skips. No BLOCKER, HIGH, MEDIUM, or LOW finding remains open. Only informational notes are recorded (the stale-case provider failure is inherently never contacted because the reader does not refresh while an entry is usable; the concurrency test is timing-based but stable; Sonarr concurrency is covered by the provider-level shared gate rather than a Sonarr-specific test). Reviewer status: PASS.

findings.summary: CLOSED and mutation-verified: the stale-but-usable boundary is now served as bounded last-known-good with the provider failing and no request, and the expired boundary is evicted with the provider actually read and a bounded failure returned.
findings.description: RadarrStaleObservationSetIsServedWithoutAProviderCallWhenTheProviderFails stores an observation 45s old under a 1-minute TTL (fresh for 30s, stale-usable until 60s), points the responder at failure, and reads the identity: it asserts success, the quality label, no request, and one retained connection. RadarrExpiredObservationSetIsEvictedAndTheProviderFailureIsBounded stores an observation 90s old (> StaleUntil), and the reader actually issues one /api/v3/movie request, returns the ProviderUnavailable/Later failure, and retains nothing. Both were driven through the real reader/cache boundary (no injected clock needed; the entry is constructed at a chosen observation time).

findings.summary: CLOSED and mutation-verified: per-connection single-flight coalescing is implemented and tested under a real concurrent cold start; removing the shared gate fails the test deterministically.
findings.description: ArrInventoryCacheProvider owns a per-connection SemaphoreSlim(1,1) population gate; the readers acquire it on a cold cache, re-check the cache inside it, then populate once. ConcurrentColdReadersShareOneLibraryRead launches four cold readers against a blocking handler and asserts LibraryRequestCount == 1; ProviderFailureReleasesThePopulationGateForALaterAttempt drives a failed population then a successful later attempt. The gate is an async semaphore (no monitor lock across provider I/O), cancellation-aware, and lease-disposed on every path.
verification: Mutation M4 (throwaway): AcquirePopulationAsync returns a fresh per-call semaphore instead of the shared per-connection gate. Expected failure observed: ConcurrentColdReadersShareOneLibraryRead FAIL in 3/3 consecutive runs (19 passed each run).
findings.recommended_action: None; closed. The timing-based detection mechanism is noted as informational TQ-11.2-A2-2.

findings.summary: The stale-case failing responder is never contacted, by design: while a usable entry exists the reader does not consult the provider at all.
findings.description: The reader has no code path that attempts a refresh and then falls back to a retained entry on failure; bounded last-known-good is preserved precisely because no provider call is made while the entry is usable. The stale test therefore establishes 'a stale-but-usable entry is served without contacting the provider (even when it is failing)', and the expired test establishes the actual read-attempt-and-bounded-failure path. Together they fully account for the documented behavior; the test name mentions the failing provider as the condition, which is accurate but could be read as implying a refresh attempt.
evidence: src/ArrTags/Providers/Radarr/RadarrMetadataReader.cs:83-88 (usable entry returns before any client call); no WithFailure call site in either reader.
findings.recommended_action: None required. The behavior is accurately documented and both boundaries are mutation-sensitive.

findings.summary: The concurrent cold-start test is timing-based but stable and mutation-sensitive on this environment.
findings.description: ConcurrentColdReadersShareOneLibraryRead waits for the first library request and then Task.Delay(250) before releasing the blocking handler, so a non-coalesced implementation has time to issue redundant reads. It ran green 5/5 focused-class runs and 10/10 targeted runs, and the M4 no-coalescing mutation failed 3/3 runs. No false-pass or flake was observed. This is inherent to concurrency testing and does not undermine the verdict; on an extremely slow host the delay could theoretically mask a broken gate only in the mutant, not in the shipped suite.
evidence: M4: 3/3 mutant runs failed; pristine 5x focused + 10x targeted all green.

findings.summary: Concurrent cold-start coalescing is tested through the Radarr reader only; the Sonarr reader relies on the same provider-level gate.
findings.description: The single-flight gate is owned by ArrInventoryCacheProvider and is provider-agnostic; both readers call the same AcquirePopulationAsync and perform the same re-check. The concurrency test uses Radarr, and the Sonarr reader's use of the gate is exercised indirectly by the sequential Sonarr cache/retention tests. A Sonarr-specific concurrent cold-start test would duplicate the same provider code path.

summary: The correction round genuinely closes all six attempt-1 test-quality findings, independently confirmed by mutation testing in a throwaway /tmp copy: TQ-11.2-1 (both stale-served and expired-evicted provider-boundary directions fail under their respective mutations), TQ-11.2-2 (Sonarr fallback disabled fails), TQ-11.2-3 (single-record cache fails Radarr and Sonarr whole-library retention), TQ-11.2-4 (shared gate removed fails concurrent cold-start deterministically 3/3), TQ-11.2-5 (single-id Sonarr selector fails), and TQ-11.2-6 (current-suite counts refreshed to 1,407/63/1,470, matching my reproduction). The new RC8 chunking behavior is implemented in both bulk clients and its test is mutation-sensitive. The suite is 20 unguarded [Fact]s with 0 skips; the default suite is 1,407/63/1,470 with 0 failures; the host-guarded and forced-native suites remain not runnable in this environment under pre-existing documented guards. No open BLOCKER, HIGH, MEDIUM, or LOW finding remains; three informational notes record that the stale-case provider is inherently never contacted, that the concurrency test is timing-based but stable and mutation-sensitive, and that Sonarr concurrency is covered by the shared provider-level gate.
